evidence: src/application/task-service.ts: create() builds a Task through its domain constructor using the injected IdGenerator and Clock ports, then calls this.tasks.save(task). This is orchestration through ports, not a persistence implementation.
src/application/task-service.ts: assign() and markDone() hand state changes to the domain methods task.assignTo(userId) and task.markDone(this.clock.now()), so the business rules stay in the domain.

src/application/task-service.ts: requireProject() and requireTask() only check that entities exist and that the task belongs to the project via repository lookups, which is an application-level use-case precondition.
src/application/task-service.ts: results are mapped with toTaskDto, which is application-layer output shaping. There are no HTTP status codes, request or response objects, or serialization concerns.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskService is an application-layer use-case orchestrator. Its methods load aggregates through repository interfaces, check that referenced entities exist and raise NotFoundError, delegate state changes to domain methods (task.assignTo, task.markDone), save through ports, and map results to DTOs. It has no persistence implementation, no HTTP or transport handling, no framework code, and no embedded business invariants: the transition rules stay in the Task entity. The only checks are existence lookups and project-scoping lookups, which are typical application-layer orchestration. No ADR prose was provided.
